newsitem.title: UK: Pacific freight rates stimulate market sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Pacific freight rates stimulate market sentiment.

text.p: More active chartering of panamaxes in the Pacific was helping to bolster market sentiment although actual rates being paid were still mixed.

"Bullish sentiment without many bullish rates," was how one broker summed up today's panamax market. He added that "the best news in the Atlantic is that vessels are being fixed in the Pacific", thus protecting atlantic rates from tonnage ballasting into the US Gulf.
Pacific rates continued to be the main impetus behind the rise in the BFI, up 6 points today to 1023, making a total of 31 points since the index turned higher on Sept 26.
Meanwhile capers continued out of favour in a market described by an owner's broker as "unadulterated rubbish".

GRAIN - A number of vessels were reported fixed in the US Gulf/Far East grain trades but conflicting rumours surfaced today which made the immediate course of freight rates difficult for brokers to read.

On the one hand EMC paid $20.25 no combo for 54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan, superficially a stronger level but not a great premium for a forward position, and on the other rumours circulated that MOSK had fixed under $20.00 no combo and Halla had booked Chinese tonnage at $19.50, both for first half nov.
Others reported that $20.25 no combo was available in the market for early Nov and had not been taken by owners.

From the North Pacific Toepfer were linked with Rani Padmini for 55,000 barley to Saudi Arabia for end Oct at $15.00, and Continental were believed to have taken CSK Unity 68,371 dwt for grain to S.Korea on private terms.
In the handy-sizes Toepfer were rumoured to have covered about 1.2m cft US Gulf/Ireland at about $12.50, and US Gulf/Liverpool and Plate/Bangkok on private terms.

MINERALS - The Kepco coal tender led to 3 capers fixed on timecharter: Turtle Queen 146,000 dwt delivery Japan end Oct for a Dalrymple round at $8,500 daily to Korea Line (against Kepco's voyage rate in the low $5.00's), La Pampa 139,000 dwt on private terms to Hanjin for a Port Kembla round (against a voyage rate in the low $6.00's), and Bulktirreno 145,856 dwt to HMM also on private terms for an Abbots Point round (against a voyage rate to Kujung at $5.50).

Panamax coal business included reports of Delphic Pride booked by Cobelfret for 55,000 Richards Bay/Morocco at close to $6.50. Alescabalo 70,402 dwt was rumoured fixed China/Hongkong, and an unnamed panamax for Baltimore/Bourgas, both on private terms.

NYK were said to have covered about 55,000 bauxite Weipa/Puerto Vesme at $9.75. Previous reports of AIMR's fixture of Avalon 73,080 dwt with Long Beach petcoke to the Continent were incorrect - $4,300 daily for the first 30 days followed by $7,500 daily plus $115,000 bonus were the rates understood to be closer to the facts.

HANDY-SIZES - reports of greater activity surfaced from the far east. Star fixed a 35,000 dwt vessel delivery S.E.Asia for an Australian round at $7,000 daily and MOSK fixed a 43,338 dwt craned bulker on subjects from Kalimantan to Japan at $7,750 daily.

Pisces Planter 35,310 dwt was fixed on subjects from Nopac to the far east by Canpotex but further details were lacking. M and R booked Atlas 37,365 dwt from Richards Bay to the Continent for Oct 15/25 at only $4,500 daily.
